It has no antecedent — 'what' means 'the thing which'. This is why 'the thing what I said' is wrong: the noun is already inside the 'what'. 'Whoever wrote this' and 'wherever it came from' work the same way.

grammar.label: reduced relative clauses and participial postmodification
grammar.form: noun + present participle / past participle / to-infinitive (+ rest)
grammar.meaning: packs a whole clause into a phrase after the noun

explanation.en: 'The people who were waiting outside' becomes 'the people waiting outside'; 'the road that was built in 1954' becomes 'the road built in 1954'; 'the first man who reached the summit' becomes 'the first man to reach the summit'. The reduced form is possible only when the relative pronoun is the subject of its clause. 'The report that I read' cannot reduce.
explanation.uz: 'The people who were waiting outside' → 'the people waiting outside'. Qisqartirish faqat bog'lovchi olmosh o'z gapining egasi bo'lgandagina mumkin. 'The report that I read' qisqartirilmaydi.

grammar.label: nominal relative clauses — what, whoever, wherever as noun phrases
grammar.form: what / whatever / whoever / wherever / however + clause, filling a noun slot
grammar.meaning: names a thing by describing it instead of naming it

explanation.en: A nominal relative is a whole clause doing a noun's job: 'What the committee decided' is the subject of 'surprised everyone'. It has no antecedent — 'what' means 'the thing which'. This is why 'the thing what I said' is wrong: the noun is already inside the 'what'. 'Whoever wrote this' and 'wherever it came from' work the same way.
explanation.uz: Nominal relative — butun gap ot vazifasini bajaradi: 'What the committee decided surprised everyone'. 'What' = 'the thing which', shuning uchun 'the thing what I said' xato: ot allaqachon 'what' ichida.

grammar.positive_example: Whoever drafted this clause understood the law better than we do.
grammar.negative_example: The person whoever drafted this clause understood the law.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida bu -gan/-adigan qo'shimchali sifatdosh bilan beriladi; boshqaruvchi ot qo'shib yuborish keng tarqalgan xato.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: My teachers keep asking me what a morpheme is.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The smallest part of a word that carries meaning. 'Unhappy' has two.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Do they need the word at all?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: They need it once. After that they need the idea, which is that English builds words out of parts and Uzbek builds them out of endings.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That is a better definition than the one in the book.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The book defines the term and never says why anyone should care.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: There is a line in my report with the same fault. 'Every district affected by the flood received a payment.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: That line is fine. 'Affected by the flood' is a reduced relative and it saves three words.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Which would mean the districts did the flooding. The participle has to face the right way.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: And 'whoever drafted this clause knew the law better than we do'?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Also right, and note what you did not write: 'the person whoever drafted it'. The noun is already inside the 'whoever'.
